enrichment.markdown:
**Yitzhak Mentzel / Menchel:** I did not find a reliable outside-archive identification for this person under **Yitzhak, Isaac, Itzik, or איציק**, or the spellings **Mentzel, Menczel, Menchel,** and **Mentshel**. Searches included Yad Vashem, USHMM, Arolsen Archives, JewishGen’s Skala KehilaLinks pages, and Geni. Without a matching record, I can’t establish his dates, family relationships, or fate from outside sources.

**Sarah Wiesenthal:** The Skala KehilaLinks family history describes a Sarah who had emigrated to New York, returned to Skala around 1929–30, married **Moshe Efraim (Morris) Wiesenthal**, and then emigrated with him to New York. It says Morris was born in 1902, was the son of Zechariah and Brucha Wiesenthal, owned a Bronx grocery store, and died in Florida in 1985. The page does not give Sarah’s surname before marriage or establish that she is the Sarah Wiesenthal connected to this record, so that identification remains uncertain. ([Skala KehilaLinks, “Polish Army”](https://kehilalinks.jewishgen.org/SkalaPodol/PolishArmy.html); [“Love, Skala Style”](https://kehilalinks.jewishgen.org/SkalaPodol/LoveSkalaStyle.html))

**Menchel family connection:** A Skala family-history page names **Moses Efroim Menchel** (born 1880), son of **Maryam Wiesenthal** and **Mendel Menchel**, and his wife **Rivka Menchel**. It reports that both died in Skala in 1942, perhaps in the September action. This is a promising Menchel/Wiesenthal lead, but the source does not identify Moses as Yitzhak’s relative; the similar surname alone cannot prove a connection. ([Skala KehilaLinks, “Wiesenthal Relatives from Skala who Perished in the Holocaust”](https://kehilalinks.jewishgen.org/SkalaPodol/Wiesenthal_relatives_perish.html))

That same page traces Wiesenthal relatives across Skala and nearby wartime destinations: some were deported to the Borszczów ghetto or Tluste, some were murdered at Bełżec, and some escaped or emigrated. These accounts provide family and community context, but do not independently establish any relationship to Yitzhak or the Sarah named in the record. The page is a Skala research-group family compilation, not an individual archival document. ([same family-history page](https://kehilalinks.jewishgen.org/SkalaPodol/Wiesenthal_relatives_perish.html))

sources.title: Skala KehilaLinks, “Wiesenthal Relatives from Skala who Perished in the Holocaust”
